newsitem.title: INDIA: India soybean arrivals low as farmer hold stocks.
newsitem.headline: India soybean arrivals low as farmer hold stocks.

text.p: Indian soybean arrivals remained sluggish in the domestic market as farmers held back stocks to sell later at higher prices, traders said on Tuesday.
They said soybean arrivals were currently around 1,000 tonnes per day compared with 15,000 tonnes per day in the same time a year earlier in the central Indian markets, the hub of soybean industry.
Traders said soybean was currently quoted at 12,200-12,500 rupees per tonne.
"Farmers are hoping that they can get at least 13,000-13,000 per tonne this year," said Prakash Vohra, a leading oilmeal trader.
Traders said poor availability of soybean had forced processing plants to switch to rapeseed crushing as rapeseed extraction was in good export demand.
They said rapeseed extraction was currently quoted at $115 per tonne FAS against around $90 per tonne same period last year.
Traders said Indian exporters had so far contracted to export 2.2 million tonnes of soymeal which was about 1.9 million tonnes same period a year ago.
Soymeal for exports was quoted at $305 per tonne FAS against $220 at the same time last year.
